_comment: Mutation testing: breaks the source on purpose and checks the tests notice. A mutant that
leaves the suite green is a bug the tests cannot see — unlike line coverage, this cannot be
satisfied by executing code without asserting on it.
Full explanation, glossary and diagrams: docs/tools/mutation-testing.md. This file carries
only the reasoning behind the settings below.
A run re-executes the suite once per mutant, so it lives in .github/workflows/mutation.yml,
nightly and on demand. The PR-time gate is `npm run test:mutation:check`, which compares the
last report against mutation-baseline.json in under a second and runs no mutants at all.
`mutate` covers services, models, repositories, middlewares, jobs and core. A file absent
from the report reads exactly like a file with no survivors, so anything excluded must be
excluded for a stated reason:
- CONTROLLERS are out because of the RUNNER, not because they are unimportant. Only the
unit suite runs here; controllers are covered through tests/contract and
tests/integration, so under this runner every controller mutant would survive and 35
files would report ~0%. That number would measure the instrument, not the code, and the
ratchet would then defend those zeros forever. Putting them in scope requires first
deciding to run contract/integration under Stryker — an hours-per-run decision, not a glob.
- core/bootstrap/** wires up the process (env parsing, OTel SDK, server lifecycle, database
connection). Its mutants ask whether the suite boots a differently-configured process,
which these unit tests cannot answer.
- core/observability/tracer.ts is OTel span plumbing; a mutated attribute name changes
nothing observable without an exporter to read back.
`ignorePatterns` must NOT list public/**: the sandbox is the only filesystem the tests see,
and tests/unit/db/seed-fixtures.test.ts asserts every seed fixture's imageUrl resolves to a
committed file under public/images/seed/. Without it Stryker refuses to start at all.
Green at 80+, yellow 60-80, red and failing below 60. `break` sits at the bottom of the band
deliberately, so the gate answers 'has something collapsed' rather than 'did the number move'.
The real gate is per-FILE, in mutation-baseline.json — a global percentage lets a strong file
carry a weak one. Raise `break` only when a score SUSTAINS a higher band; never lower it to
make a run pass.
Read `total` against `covered` before spending effort. Far apart means mutants with NO
COVERAGE — write tests that reach the code. Close together means tests run it without
asserting — sharpen what exists. Different work; the single percentage hides which.
The ceiling is MEMORY, not cores: each worker is a separate process carrying a full test
runner and its own in-memory mongod, and the machine is in use while a run happens. 8 on a
32-core / 30 GB box leaves headroom deliberately; at 12, free RAM fell to ~6 GB and load
average hit 14. Lower it on a smaller machine rather than raising it on a bigger one.
CI overrides this: mutation.yml passes --concurrency 3, because a standard GitHub runner is
4 vCPU / 16 GB. The safe number is a property of the machine, not of the project.
A run strands one ~200 MB mongo-mem-* directory in /tmp per killed worker (Stryker SIGKILLs
a jest worker per timed-out mutant, so MongoMemoryServer.stop() never runs).
tests/helpers/global-setup.ts prunes the directories whose mongod is provably gone, never a
concurrent instance's live one — read that file before changing the sweep.
72.65% total / 76.51% of covered code, 2685 mutants, ~36 minutes at concurrency 8.
mutation-baseline.json holds the per-file figures and is the thing to read; this total is
context, not a target.
Weakest files worth attention: core/adapters/pdf.ts, core/observability/stream.ts and
core/observability/metrics-domain.ts all sit at 0% — genuinely untested by any suite, and
recording that honestly is the point of the scope above. Then models/audit-logs.ts (36.73%),
core/observability/metrics-http.ts (48.76%), repositories/feedback-requests.ts (54.55%).
middlewares/security.ts (41.67%) is NOT on that list despite the number: its survivors are
the two rateLimit({...}) option literals, where mutating windowMs changes nothing any test
can observe without waiting out a real window. Its one real decision — isMetricsScraper, the
credential check on the Prometheus endpoint — is fully covered. Leave it.
